newsitem.title: INDIA: INDIAN HEADLINE STOCKS - factors to watch - Feb 21.
newsitem.headline: INDIAN HEADLINE STOCKS - factors to watch - Feb 21.

text.p: Following are some of the main factors affecting Indian stock markets on Friday morning:
NEWS OUTLOOK:

** India's main opposition party on Thursday backtracked on a bid to topple Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda, saying it would not press for a no-confidence vote against the government it had planned for Friday.
"We are not interested in a no-confidence motion early
in the budget session," former prime minister Atal Behari Vajpayee, the leader of the biggest opposition group, the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP), told Reuters. "We want it as the last weapon."

** India's Disinvestment Commission, which oversees partial privatisation, on Thursday recommended the sale of shares in three state firms and the setting up of a pool to club funds raised by divestment.
It said the government should sell 25 percent of its
stake in the Gas Authority of India Ltd (GAIL), 100 percent of Modern Food Industries (India) Ltd and 74 percent or more of the India Tourism Development Corporation (ITDC).
** Tax concessions make India's infrastructure policy attractive, but political confusion and bureaucratic bungling are putting off foreign investors, analysts said on Thursday.
They said politicans of the ruling United Front
coalition were shifting from commitments on specific issues, affecting tax incentives designed to lure billions of dollars to build roads, airports, power plants, ports and telecommunications.
** Consumer electrical major Philips India on Thursday announced a 65.0 percent fall in 1996 net profit to 80.70 million rupees against 229.1 million rupees in the year-ago period.
The firm's sales slipped to 14.85 billion rupees from
15,20 billion rupees in the previous year. The company slashed 1996 dividend to 1.0 rupees per share from 2.5 rupees last year.
"Slowdown in the economy and depressed market
conditions, especially in consumer electronics caused lower sales," Philips India said in a statement.
MARKETS:
** The Indian rupee opened unchanged at 35.88/89 against the dollar on Friday. The day's range seen at 35.88/90 rupees to a dollar, dealers said.
** Indian stocks suffered minor losses on Thursday in a session that largely lacked direction, said traders.
** The benchmark 30-share index of the Bombay Stock Exchange ended 34.24 points, or 0.97 percent, down at 3,494.20.
** The 50-stock National Stock Exchange index slumped 8.75 points, or 0.86 percent, to 1,003.10.
** The Delhi share index fell 5.53 points to 735.44.
** The Calcutta share index slumped 2.05 points to 448.87.
** The Madras share index was down 2.23 points to 3,372.65.
